- **Rationale.** D19 asks for "a reported non-blocking mode or a separate presenter if only FIFO is available"; deferral (round 3) left the secondary window undrawn for the whole run, which CodeRabbit raised twice. The hand-off keeps the render thread free of every blocking secondary call: it only takes a free slot, renders, submits and posts. The pool of three covers one frame rendering, one queued and one presenting, so `Busy` only appears when the presenter falls behind, and latest-wins keeps the secondary display at most one frame stale. `force_presenter_thread` makes the path testable on CI adapters (lavapipe, Metal, WARP) that offer Mailbox: `presenter_thread_window` drives it end to end on real windows, `wiring_render` checks both the COPY_DST copy and the blit texel for texel against the offscreen frame, and the hand-off, bounded join, detach-with-guard and panic-close semantics are pure unit tests.
- **Alternatives.** (a) Keep deferral: rejected (the window stays undrawn; D19 names the presenter). (b) A `pin_render` API for table textures on its `SurfaceSet` presenter threads: rejected for this round, it needs a `pin_render` change while `pin_app` can do it alone with public wgpu types and `spawn_guarded`. (c) A blocking `sync_channel(1)` per surface like `pin_render`'s debug presenter: rejected, a full channel either blocks the render thread or needs a separate busy flag, and it has no latest-wins replacement. (d) Draw the secondary surface from the render thread at reduced cadence: rejected in round 3 (a Fifo acquire can still stall the playfield). Untested on CI: a real FIFO-only secondary swap chain on hardware (no CI adapter offers one); to be checked at acceptance (D31).

## 5.4 — CodeRabbit round 1 (PR #22)

**Decision.**
- Shader translation (finding 6): naga 30.0.1 translates `trace.wgsl` to HLSL and to MSL 2.4 without error; the default MSL version is rejected ("ray tracing is not supported prior to MSL 2.4"). `tests/raytrace_naga.rs` now asserts all three. This supersedes the "MSL/HLSL outcome printed, not asserted" wording of the earlier 5.4 section (that section is left unedited; this one is the correction). wgpu is not claimed to use these back ends for ray queries.
- Survey wording (finding 1): the module docs and test docs now state only what was observed: Vulkan (lavapipe) reports `EXPERIMENTAL_RAY_QUERY`; GL does not; the hosted Windows (DX12/WARP) and macOS (Metal) runners did not in the Q3 spike. The ray path is taken only when the device reports and enables the feature. DX12 and Metal on real hardware are open (PLAN risk row 5).
- Device loss (finding 3, implemented in `raytrace/`): wgpu 30.0.1 DOES have `Device::set_device_lost_callback`, so the earlier "wgpu 30 has no device-lost query" statement (the earlier 5.4 section and `select.rs`) is corrected. `RayQueryReflections` registers the callback; on loss it stops rendering and returns `Err` from `prepare` instead of rendering probes on the dead device. Trace errors on a live device still fall back to probes. `GpuError` has no `DeviceLost` variant (adding one is a breaking change to an earlier subphase), so the loss is reported as `GpuError::RequestDevice("device lost: ...")`. DEFERRED: recreating the `GpuContext`, `PbrRenderer` and probe resources after a loss, and a `GpuContext`-level lost flag, is application-lifecycle work outside `pin_render/raytrace` (HUMAN_QUEUE).
- Ball-centre jobs (finding 2, implemented in `raytrace/`): `BallCentre` jobs (rough balls above the cutoff) use the one-bounce trace so their map equals what a probe capture can show; `BallView` keeps the second bounce.
- Nitpick (`gpu/mod.rs` duplicated adapter/device request flow): deferred (HUMAN_QUEUE).
- Test strictness (findings 4, 5): `spec_5_4_gpu` now fails when context creation fails under `PIN_REQUIRE_RAY_QUERY=1` (as under `PIN_REQUIRE_GPU=1`), and asserts exactly 2 BLAS builds and 1 TLAS refit after the first frame.

**Rationale.** Docs and tests must claim only what was observed; a required-GPU run must not pass without executing; `gpu/mod.rs` belongs to an earlier subphase and 5.4 may only add the constructor; rebuild after loss needs app lifecycle work.

**Alternatives.** Keep the Vulkan-only claim (rejected: unestablished). Refactor `gpu/mod.rs` now (rejected: shared by every GPU test and the windowed path). Add `GpuError::DeviceLost` (rejected: breaking change to an earlier subphase).

## 5.4 — CodeRabbit round 1 (PR #22): device-loss details (addendum)
- **Decision:** `RayQueryReflections` treats both `DeviceLostReason` values (`Unknown`, `Destroyed`) as a loss. It re-checks the loss flag after every trace, including a successful one, because wgpu silently drops errors raised on a lost device. wgpu keeps one device-lost callback per device, so a callback registered later (by the application or by another reflection source on the same device) replaces this one. Applications that register their own callback must forward the loss with `RayQueryReflections::mark_device_lost`.
- **Correction:** the earlier claim in this log that "wgpu 30 has no device-lost query" is wrong. wgpu 30.0.1 has `Device::set_device_lost_callback`; it still has no polling query.
- **Rationale:** dropping a device never invokes the callback in wgpu-core 30.0.1, so ordinary teardown raises no false alarm. Re-checking after a successful trace closes the gap where a trace on a dead device reports Ok.
- **Alternatives:** a `GpuContext`-level loss flag and rebuilding the context, `PbrRenderer` and the reflection source after a loss. Both are deferred; see HUMAN_QUEUE.

## vuk-remove-ball — hold release on ball removal
- **Decision.** `MechSet::release_ball(h)` (new, `pin_physics/src/mech`) clears `held` on every VUK whose `held == Some(h)`; VUK holds are the only per-ball (slot-keyed) mech state (bumpers, slingshots, sliders, plungers, drops and spinners keep none). `Simulation::remove_slot` calls it right after `BallSolver::remove_ball` succeeds, so `Simulation::remove_ball` and the tick's drain / escape path both release the hold before any ball can be added to the freed slot. The release does not touch the mech's switch state: the VUK switch opens at the next `post_step` with the normal Opened edge. Runs that never remove a held ball are unchanged (the call is a no-op), so their replay digests are identical. Allocation-free (a loop over the fixed mech vector), safe inside the tick.
- **Rationale.** `pin_physics` handles are slot-only (`BallHandle(u8)`), so the `solver.ball(h).is_none()` checks in `pre_step` / `post_step` cannot tell a reused slot from the held ball: a ball spawned into the slot before the next tick was pinned (or ejected, with the coil on) by the stale hold. Fixing at the removal point, where the owner of both the solver and the mechs knows the ball is gone, is exact and costs nothing per tick. A held ball reaches the drain path only when a VUK's hold point lies inside a trough zone or out of bounds (the hold pins it at the hold point); with a VUK in a trough and the rules relaunching on the trough edge, the relaunched ball was pulled into the VUK.
- **Alternatives.** (a) Store a ball generation in `held` and compare it in the tick: rejected, `pin_physics` handles are slot-only and a generation would need either a `pin_core` / `pin_physics` handle change (out of scope) or a second per-slot generation table duplicating `Simulation`'s. (b) Detect reuse in the tick (e.g. check the held ball is still at the hold point): rejected, a heuristic that a respawn at the hold point defeats. (c) Register the mech set as a solver `ExternalForce` hook to get `ball_removed`: rejected, the hooks are owned by the solver and the mech set is borrowed separately each tick.
## Orchestrator — Gate A1 criterion 1a: the analytic rolling check validates the solver
**Decision:** The 5/7·g·sinθ rolling-down-the-incline check (6.5°, 1.07 m, about 1.64 s) is evaluated two ways. (a) With rolling resistance set to 0, the acceleration matches the literal 5/7·g·sinθ (0.79323 m/s²) within 1 %. (b) With the default parameters (rolling resistance c = 0.002), the run matches 5/7·g·(sinθ − c·cosθ) within 1 %. Both must pass. The shipped default c is not changed.
**Rationale:** The literal formula has no rolling resistance. With the default c the 1.07 m run takes 1.6566 s (a = 0.77978 m/s², −1.70 % against the literal formula), but with c = 0 it is +0.06 % and against the model that includes c·cosθ it is +0.06 %. So the solver is exact and the 1.7 % comes from a deliberate default that PLAN Appendix C sets for feel. The check exists to validate the solver (Gate A1 criterion 1), so it separates the solver from the tunable. Retuning c to hit the literal number would change feel for no physical reason.
**Alternatives:** Setting default c to 0 (loses the rolling-stop behaviour that the 2.2 tests require). Widening the 1 % tolerance to 2 % (weakens the gate). Gating only the default-parameter run against the literal formula (fails with no solver defect).

## Orchestrator — Gate A1 criterion 3: median ball time is measured after the fixes, judged on skill standard, and fixed in the grey-box layout
**Decision:** (1) The 15–120 s median-ball-time window is unchanged and is not relaxed for the grey-box. It is judged on the soak at skill `standard`, the reference player; the novice and expert medians are reported. Zero stuck, escaped and non-finite balls, 100 % switch coverage and the 0.35 ms p99.9 tick are judged at all three skills. (2) Order of work: the inlane, ramp-escape and flipper dead-spot fixes land first; then the median is re-measured on 1,000 standard games; nothing else is tuned before that number exists. (3) If the re-measured median is still below 15 s, the grey-box layout (Subphase 6.0 data, `tables/greybox`) is changed to keep balls in play longer, by adding table features and guides only, such as outlane-style guards, posts, rollovers or an upfield feature the bot reaches. Physics tunables, the 6.5° slope, the 1.07 m length and the ball are not changed for this purpose, because Gate A1 holds them fixed. (4) The bot flip policy (2.9) is not tuned for ball time. (5) If a layout change moves the median without reaching the window, the next step is another layout iteration (a further 6.0 fix task), and Gate A1 stays red until the soak passes; the window is never narrowed or bypassed.
**Rationale:** The measured median is 6.7 s (about 8.7–10 s after the inlane fix), and about 3 s of every ball is plunge and travel. The causes are properties of the table: a 1.07 m table with no outlanes and few features, and escapes that end balls early (336 of 1,000 games). Gate A1 and D24 exist to validate tables with the bot, so the window describes how long a table keeps a competent player's ball. Making the standard bot flip worse to stretch ball time would be tuning to the test (rule 6 in spirit), and the bot is shared with Gate A2 and the real tables. A ruling that the window does not apply to the grey-box would remove the only soak check of play length before tables start. The grey-box is project-owned data, so adding features to it is ordinary design work. Measuring first matters because two of the three causes (escapes and stuck inlanes) are defects, and they may close much of the gap on their own.
**Alternatives:** Tuning the bot flip policy to miss more shots (tuning to the test; contaminates A2). Ruling that the window applies only to the real tables (weakens Gate A1; real tables start after A1 is green). Judging the median at the novice skill (the window then proves nothing about a competent player). Changing slope or table length (breaks the analytic checks and the Appendix C physics).

## Gate A1 — flipper dead-spot depth tuning
**Decision:** No flipper default changes. The 25 % dead-spot depth (PLAN 2.3 criterion 1, ±20 ms sweep, 50 % and 70 % contact) has no robust solution inside the Appendix C bounds, so the depth check is reported as blocked and goes back to the Orchestrator as a model question (a compliant end stop or a sweep reference that does not depend on stroke time), not a data tweak. `physics_defaults.toml` is unchanged. No candidate-parameter test was added, because pinning a knife-edge point would be tuning to the test (rule 6).
**Rationale:** Baseline depth at (inertia 1.0e-4, power 1.2, hold 0.15, spring 0.03, stop 0.15, damping 0.35):
- Tester rig (spec_2_3_criteria): 24.3 / 16.8 / 26.3 / 30.1 % at 50 / 65 / 70 / 75 % contact.
- Implementer rig (flipper_criteria, down-table, −20…+20 ms): 39.3 / 1.7 / 10.0 / 4.3 %.

Search: two release grids with overrides on `FlipperConfig`.
- Coarse grid (900 points): inertia {0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.3, 1.7}e-4 × power {1.0, 1.2, 1.5} × hold {0.08, 0.15, 0.25, 0.35} × stop {0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.25} × damping {0.25, 0.35, 0.5}. Result: 0 points pass all four straight-bat depths.
- Fine grid (6,720 points): inertia 0.85–1.2e-4 in steps of 0.05e-4, power 1.0–1.4, hold 0.05–0.4 (7 values), damping 0.1–0.7 (8 values), stop {0, 0.15, 0.4}. Result: 19 points pass all four depths with a stroke of 21 ms or more. Every one fails the ±10 % neighbour check. All but one also turn an existing test red: `flipper_criteria::dead_spot_is_an_interior_minimum_of_a_wider_sweep` (the wide-sweep conditions fail or the test panics), or `timing_sweep_has_a_dead_spot_and_no_unexplained_jumps` (max > held fails). The one exception, (1.0e-4, 1.2, 0.05, 0.0, 0.35 → damping 0.5), has margins of 0.5 % (A70 24.5 %) and 0.2 % (B50 24.8 %), and fails with damping ±10 % or hold +10 %.

Mechanism: the dead flip is the one whose stroke ends in the tick the ball arrives, at about −(stroke time) ms. The stroke is 21 ms at the defaults, and the implementer test needs at least 21 ms (feel window 20–35 ms, EOS still closed one tick earlier). So the dead spot sits at the −20 ms edge of the sweep. +10 % inertia or −10 % power gives a 22 ms stroke, the dead spot leaves the window, and the 50 % depth jumps to 48–63 %. Inside the 21 ms band the depth swings 5–10 points with the sub-tick phase, so passing points are isolated. Stop restitution has almost no effect, because the ball meets the bat before or as it reaches the stop.
**Alternatives:** (a) Ship the closest passing point (1.2e-4, 1.3, hold 0.11): A50 22.6 / A70 16.5 / B50 24.4 / B70 1.5 %. Rejected: knife-edge (inertia ±10 % and power ±10 % fail), it adds unexplained steps in the B rig at 65 % and 70 %, and it turns `dead_spot_is_an_interior_minimum_of_a_wider_sweep` (70 %) red. (b) Ship the only point that keeps the wide-sweep test green (1.0e-4, 1.2, 0.05, 0.0, 0.5). Rejected: margins of 0.2–0.5 %, it fails damping ±10 %, and hold sits at its lower bound. (c) A solver change (compliant end stop, Subphase 2.3 T2/T3) or a ruling on the sweep reference, for example centring the sweep on the stroke-end tick. Left to the Orchestrator.

## Orchestrator — Gate A1: the 25 % dead-spot depth is reported, not gating, until an end-stop compliance model exists
**Decision:** Gate A1 passes or fails on the items PLAN's Gate A1 text lists: the analytic checks; the feel windows for unloaded stroke time, cradled full-shot exit speed and, from Appendix C, bumper and sling kick exit speed; and the soak criteria. The 25 % dead-spot depth (moved here by "2.3 criterion 1: the 25 % depth moves to Gate A1") stays a measured and reported A1 metric for every rig and contact. It does not gate A1 while the flipper has a rigid end stop. The follow-up is a model task owned by 2.3: a compliant end stop, or a sweep reference that does not depend on stroke time. After that lands, the depth becomes gating, and Gate A1 re-runs.
**Rationale:** The bounded search ("Gate A1 — flipper dead-spot depth tuning") shows that no settings inside the Appendix C bounds meet the depth robustly. The dead flip ends its stroke in the tick the ball arrives, so the depth is set by sub-tick phase (5–10 points of swing within one tick) and by the rig. The few passing points fail their ±10 % neighbours, and all but one break existing flipper tests. Pinning one would be tuning to the test (rule 6). The earlier ruling already expected that "an end-stop compliance if a later subphase adds one" might be needed. Appendix C marks the feel windows as provisional and reviewed at final acceptance. Blocking every Wave 7 table on a model change that is not yet scheduled would stall the plan (D28).
**Alternatives:** Keep the depth gating, so A1 stays red until a solver change to the end stop: very-high blast radius, every replay fixture changes, and Fable allowance is unknown. Accept a knife-edge default (rule 6). Change the sweep reference now (redefines the metric without a model reason).

## Gate A1 — drop-bounce measurement: post-impact velocity and phase-averaged apex

**Decision.** The Gate A1 1b drop-bounce tests (`crates/pin_physics/tests/a1_analytic.rs`) measure restitution as the normal velocity at the end of the impact tick divided by the Impact event's `normal_speed` (guarded: exactly one event, an Impact, on that tick; cross-checked by the median of `vs[k] + gn (k - k0) dt` over k0..k0+5), asserted within 1 % of the pair-table e on the flat and the 6.5 degree floor, for every pair and both drop heights. The height ratio uses a phase-averaged apex: 20 drops spread evenly over one tick of fall phase (`drop + k v_impact dt / 20`), mean apex/drop compared with e^2 within 2 %. The analytic correction (H = w(1-phi)h + (w - g h/2)^2 / (2g)) was not needed. Measured mean height-ratio errors: flat +0.005 to +0.164 %, pitched -0.032 to -0.090 %; speed ratio error under 0.001 % everywhere. The pitched test is now gating (`drop_bounce_on_the_pitched_playfield_restitution`), plus a 100-drop phase sweep (50.00 to 51.98 mm, steel/wood, flat and pitched). No solver change was made.

**Rationale.** The apex method carried a tick-phase bias of g h (1/2 - phi) from the semi-implicit Euler integrator (gravity applied at sub-step boundaries), about +-1.9 % in speed and +-4.8 % in height ratio over a 2 mm sweep of drop heights, on flat and pitched floors alike. An issue-investigator showed the solver is exact: post-impact normal velocity equals e times the Impact `normal_speed` to under 1e-5, and pitched-floor deviations were identical with friction 0 and with gravity along -n only. So the earlier -1.1 % / -2.8 % pitched deviation was a measurement artefact, not a defect.

**Alternatives.** Exact parabolic drift in the integrator, which would remove the phase bias but change every trajectory and every pinned hash: rejected. Keeping the single-drop apex estimate with a wider tolerance: rejected (tolerances are not loosened).

## 6.0 fix — Gate A1 grey-box geometry

**Decision.** Data-only fixes in `tables/greybox` (no engine code):
- Inlanes end on the back of the flipper pivot caps: left `[[0,330],[152,172]]`, right `[[470,330],[362,172]]` (was `[140,160]` / `[374,160]`, which left a V-pocket that held balls).
- Drain: the right funnel wall runs `(357,150) → (335,0)` (was `→ (299,10)`, leaving a pocket beside `trough_2` at (318,14)); `trough_1` (225,20) r 34 and `trough_2` (289,20) r 34 (were (240,35)/(274,35) r 25): symmetric about x 257 (a centre drain still closes both) and covering the whole funnel bottom (ball centres x 192..322).
- `drop_1` faces 290° (was 270°): a ball rolling down onto its back rolled to rest there (novice soak); tilted, it rolls off.
- Ramp entry (Fix A + B): a 40 mm layer-0 lane, x 405..445, on the wire's axis x 425. The right wall reaches down to y 430; the left wall starts at y 545 with a funnel wall from (370,485), so the mouth takes a ball rolling straight up at x 420 (the `greybox_game` injection) and the left flipper's 25..35° shots, which glance off the right wall. The lane walls end on a roof `(405,640) → (470,660)` that slopes down to the left from the shooter-lane wall. `entry_width` 40 makes the generated 0 → 2 zone x 405..445, y 575..615 (exactly the lane). A layer-2 floor (deck, z 0.1) under x 403..447, y 560..692.5 carries a promoted ball until the rails take it. `ramp_fallback` (2 → 0) is x 375..465, y 350..574 (ends 1 mm below the entry zone, so it never contains a just-promoted ball). Catch zones 2 → 0 from y 575 to 890: `ramp_catch_left` x 325..403, `ramp_catch_right` x 447..525 (z −50..200), `ramp_catch_below` x 403..447, z ≤ 9.
- Wire: gauge 13 (was 19; contact 29° from vertical, inside the validator's 20..75°), points y 595..905 at x 425, rails from −6 mm (below the floor) rising to 51.5/51.8 mm over the deck, level at the end; the ball meets the rails from below at y ~662, there is no rail end to strike. Layer-2 side rails (`ramp_side_left/right`, guides at x 405/445, bottom edge 6 mm below the rails). `ramp_exit` (2 → 1) x 395..455, y 875..950, z 30..140. Covers (decks) at z 80: layer 2 over x 403..447, y 800..905 and layer 1 over x 395..455, y 870..960.
- Upper deck z 50 (was 60): deck rails, `deck_opto` and the VUK `exit_offset` z (65) follow. Newton ball at (330,450) (was (330,380), on the line from the left flipper to the ramp). `ramp_entry` (425,560) r 16; `ramp_made` (425,868,48) r 10, near the wire's top so a ball that stalls lower does not count.

**Rationale.** Measured with the new tests (`crates/pin_app/tests/a1_inlane.rs`, `a1_ramp.rs`) and 100-game soaks: cradled left-flipper shots span 1.7..35.4° (speeds 3.6 m/s at 7° down to 2.5 m/s at 35°); only the 25..35° ones can reach the right side, and the old Newton position blocked the 29..35° lines from (220,180). The straight-up injection at x 420 in `greybox_game.rs` (must not be edited) fixes the lane on the right, so the wire stays straight up and the angled shots are turned by one glancing impact on a wood wall (e = 0.25) in a lane wide enough that the rebound does not hit the far side. Every loss on the way up counts, so the narrower gauge (less spin to gain on the rails), the lower deck (10 mm less climb) and an entry right after the impact zone were chosen. The covers stop fast balls (4 m/s) that leave the rails where they level out from flying over the deck rail. Escapes on the approach sweep went from 33 of 75 (unfixed) to 0; soak seed 1: 0 StuckBall / 0 EscapedBall / 0 NonFinite at all three skills, ramp made 12 / 9 / 2 times (novice / standard / expert).

**Alternatives.** (a) Turning the wire's first section towards the left flipper's line: the lane would leave x 420 (breaks the unchanged `greybox_game` ramp injection) and runs into the shooter-lane wall within 100 mm. (b) A 30 mm lane with a slanted funnel or a two-stage right wall: the rebound hit the funnel at 40° and the ball stalled on the wire (v1/v2 in the investigation). (c) Narrowing the lane on layer 2 with guides: the guides are steel (e ≈ 0.8) and threw the ball across the lane. (d) Upper deck at z 40: more ramp makes, but the escape bound (collider bounds + 50 mm, so wire top + 50 mm) dropped to 94 mm and a ball launched by the drop target's reset reached 94 mm. (e) Lane walls up to y 800 to close layer 0 under the whole low wire: balls dropping off the upper deck landed on the roof and bounced into a bumper in the air; the roof now ends at y 660 and layer-0 balls pass under the wire's 0..20 mm section (visual only, layers do not collide). (f) Fixing the generated entry zone in `pin_tablegen`: out of this brief (see the HUMAN_QUEUE follow-up).

## 6.0 fix — grey-box play length (Gate A1 median)

**Decision.** Blocked: no grey-box layout change is applied. Within this brief's constraints (flippers, bumpers, slings, rules, physics, slope and length unchanged; every existing pin_app test passing unmodified), no layout tried puts the standard median ball time at 15 s or more. Measured before any change (`measure` step, 1,000 games, standard, seed 1, a1/fix e950670): median 10,491 ms, p90 30,304 ms, p99 57,584 ms. The soak report has no p10; a 100-game probe gave about 4.0 s. 0 findings. Design runs (standard, seed 1, 200 games unless stated):
- (1) Orbit lane rerouted to end at (85, 615) above the upper-left flipper, with `orbit_entry` moved to (38, 700). Every plunge rides the orbit backwards, so this feeds the upper flipper instead of the left inlane. With walls 50 mm and a deck-exit guide wall (468,860)–(372,800) onto `bumper_2`: 14,561 ms, 0 findings. Adding a wall (470,395)–(445,430) that closes the alcove right of the ramp lane: 16,333 ms, 1 StuckBall at (323, 14).
- (2) Centre guard post (255, 200) r 6, rubber, with walls 50 mm, the deck guide and trough radii 36: 26,306 ms (2 EscapedBall). With (1) as well: 31,773 ms (1,000 games: 32,017 ms, 3 EscapedBall, tick p99.9 105.6 µs).
- Without (1) and (2): walls 50, deck guide and alcove wall give 11,576 ms. Posts at (255, 290) and (255, 320) give 11,321 and 11,114 ms. A post at (255, 165) nearly closes the drain: games ran to max ticks, so the run was stopped.
- A plunge deflector (276,1046)–(300,1070) at the orbit's top mouth bounced weak plunges back down the shooter lane (17 of 100 games ended at max ticks with no ball drained). It also removed every `orbit_top` hit.

Why each is rejected. (1) fails `greybox_game.rs` `every_mechanism_kind_closes_its_switch`, which injects a ball at (30, 430) moving up at 2.5 m/s and expects `orbit_entry` once (line 224). Any geometry that turns the descending orbit ball towards the field also blocks that ascending ball. (2) fails `a1_bundle_feel.rs` `full_shot_from_a_cradle_exits_in_the_window_on_both_lower_flippers`: the shots from 0.72 of the bat hit the post before the 100 mm measuring point (2.371 and 2.836 m/s, window 3–7). (2) also raises drop-target hits per game from 1.45 to about 4, which exposes the drop-target reset launch. All three escapes traced came 1,000 to 1,018 ms after a `drop_1_sw` hit, which is the rules' `DROP_RESET_DELAY`. A ball kicked by `sling_right` at 2.5–3.6 m/s crosses the rising target and leaves with vz 1.2–2.35 m/s, up to z 130 mm (the ceiling) or over the cabinet wall.

**Rationale.** The window may not be relaxed. Tests may not be edited, and loosening one is not allowed (rule 6). So the outcome is reported, not forced. Most of the drains (45 % at base) are slow balls that come down the right inlane. The bot flips them near the pivot, and they dribble across the centre between the flipper tips. Only geometry near the centre line (the post) or a different plunge route (the orbit) changes that, and each of those breaks a pinned test.

**Alternatives.** (a) Update the `greybox_game` orbit injection to the rerouted lane, and accept design (1) plus another upfield feature. (b) Move the centre guard post's effect out of the feel measurement: needs a ruling on the feel test's 100 mm measuring point or on bat geometry. (c) Fix the drop-target reset launch, in the physics (edge launch off a rising kinematic box) or in rules.lua (reset only when no ball is over the target), before any longer-play design is soaked at 3 × 1,000 games. (d) Pre-existing pocket found by the alcove variant soak: a ball resting in the corner of the right funnel wall and the cabinet bottom sits at (323.3, 13.5), 34.9 mm from `trough_2` at ball height (radius 34). Trough radii 36 close it. This geometry is unchanged from the current table, so it can happen on main too.

## Orchestrator — Gate A1 median: orbit-test injection may follow a rerouted orbit; one more design iteration

**Decision.**
- The median group may move the orbit-injection start point in `crates/pin_app/tests/greybox_game.rs` (`every_mechanism_kind_closes_its_switch`, the ball fired from (30,430)) to follow a rerouted orbit lane. The test must keep its assertion unchanged: a ball travelling up the orbit lane closes `orbit_entry` exactly once. Only the injection position and heading may change.
- Trough radii go to 36 mm. This closes the measured corner gap at (323.3, 13.5), which sits 34.9 mm from `trough_2`.
- The group gets one further iteration: iteration 1, plus the alcove wall, plus r 36 troughs, plus at most one upfield feature.
- The centre guard post is rejected. It breaks the Appendix C full-shot window measured on the bundle.

**Rationale.**
- The test checks that the orbit mechanism closes its switch. The injection point is fixture data tied to the layout, so moving it with the geometry keeps what the test proves. Rule 6 forbids weakening the assertion, not repositioning a fixture.
- The trough gap is a real hazard on the current table.
- The guard post would trade one Gate A1 criterion (feel window) for another (median).

**Alternatives.**
- Relax the 15 s window or tune the bot. Rejected by the earlier criterion-3 ruling.
- Keep the injection fixed and give up the orbit reroute. That leaves about 11 s with no other layout path found in two iterations.

## a1fix bundle — cradle shot procedure

**Decision.** In `crates/pin_app/tests/a1_bundle_feel.rs` the brief's "held-down flipper" is read as the button held, so the bat is up and the cradle is at its low pivot end. "Flipper fired" is the 2.4 rig's release-then-refire full shot, with exit speed taken when the ball centre is 100 mm from the raised tip.

**Rationale.** Matches `flipper_criteria::full_shot_from_a_cradle_exits_in_the_feel_window`. Firing an already-held flipper does nothing, and with the bat at rest the pivot is its high end, so a ball cannot rest there.

**Alternatives.** Firing straight from a bat at rest with the ball near the pivot: rejected, because the ball cannot be at rest in that position.

## a1fix bundle — EOS switch sense

**Decision.** The unloaded stroke ends when the EOS switch changes state. On the grey-box the EOS switches are normally closed and open at end of stroke.

**Rationale.** Same as the pin_physics rig and `FlipperSet::eos_closed`.

**Alternatives.** None.

- Iteration 1:
